classes: What is shown versus what is used
root_cause: credential_ask_one() built the interactive password prompt from the URL's user name and host (already percent-decoded, and possibly coming from .gitmodules or a credential helper) and printed them to the terminal as they were, so control characters and terminal escape sequences in those fields could make the prompt show a trusted host other than the one the typed credentials would go to.
audit_scope: credential.c, credential.h, prompt.c and strbuf.c at the repository root
notes: Fix spans two commits: c903985 adds a host-and-port percent-encoding mode to credential_format(); 7725b81 sanitizes the prompt in credential_ask_one() and adds credential.sanitizePrompt (on by default). Order taken from the c903985 message ('An upcoming change wants to sanitize'). Released in Git 2.48.1 and the maintenance releases 2.40.4 to 2.47.2 listed in the advisory. Released January 2025. prompt.c is in audit_scope as the terminal prompt helper; it was not read.

classes: What is shown versus what is used
root_cause: At install and update Flatpak showed the permissions from the commit's xa.metadata but applied at run time the permissions in the deployed metadata file; validate_commit_metadata() and the transaction resolve code compared the two as NUL-terminated strings (ignoring everything after an embedded NUL) and only warned when xa.metadata was missing or invalid, so the permissions granted could differ from the ones shown for approval.
audit_scope: common/flatpak-transaction.c and common/flatpak-dir.c (metadata validation, transaction resolve and deploy paths)
notes: Fixed in 1.12.3 and 1.10.6, released January 2022. The advisory lists five commits; ba818f5 (size-aware comparison), d9a8f9d (fail resolve on invalid or missing xa.metadata) and 65cbfac (bundles must carry metadata) were read. 93357d3 and 54ec1a4 (unit test) are listed by short hash only and were not read. The two audit files are large; the bug lives where the shown permissions and the deployed metadata are compared.

root_cause: DefaultLinuxSpec(), SetCapabilities() and execSetPlatformOpt() filled the process's Inheritable capability set with the container's capability list instead of leaving it empty as the kernel does, so an unprivileged user inside the container who ran a program with inheritable file capabilities gained those capabilities in the permitted set across execve.
notes: 2bbc786 is the merge of the GHSA fix; OSV also names 87a90dc786bda134c9eb02adbae2c6a7342fb7f6 as the fixed commit (not read). Running containers keep the old capability sets until they are recreated. Other container runtimes had the same issue under their own advisories; they are not part of this sample.

root_cause: When a user who had received a share without download permission created or updated a reshare, ShareAPIController did not re-apply the parent share's download = false attribute to the new share (caller-supplied attributes were set after the inherited-attribute check in createShare(), and updateShare() ran its own inherited check on the node loaded from the owner's side instead of the share initiator's), so the resharer could turn download back on.
notes: Affects Nextcloud Server 24.0.4 and later 24.x, and 25.0.0; fixed in 24.0.7 and 25.0.1 (backports of PR 34502 to stable24 and stable25). PR 34502 has three commits; cf39885 holds the fix, the other two fix unit tests. The 'owner instead of initiator' wording is from the commit message; the old code path was read from the diff summary. HackerOne report 1724016 was not read.

root_cause: Http11InputBuffer.fill() switched the reused request byte buffer to write mode (position to limit, limit to capacity) before reading the socket and restored the read-mode position and limit only after a successful read, so when the read failed because the client dropped an incomplete POST, the buffer kept the wrong limit and the error response could contain bytes left from an earlier request of another user.
notes: Affects 9.0.0-M11 to 9.0.43 and 8.5.7 to 8.5.63; fixed in 9.0.44 and 8.5.64. The code was fixed in 2021 but the CVE was published in January 2024. The 8.5 fix is commit ce4b154e (short hash from the Tomcat page, not read). The fix commit message is about ReadListener.onError() on a dropped connection; the security effect is the buffer state left by the failed read.

root_cause: Request#handle_request called res_body.close as the last line of its cleanup, after uncorking the socket, closing the request body and unlinking the temp file, so an exception in any of those steps skipped closing the response body; Rack::BodyProxy callbacks such as the Rails executor then never ran, and thread-local request state (Rails CurrentAttributes) stayed on the pooled thread for the next request.
notes: Fixed in Puma 5.6.2 and 4.3.11. OSV also lists Puma commits 4ce94d7975d755f5ecdf50c5134b6d8af081e3ad and c6340d1fabcd02c4cc5c1d4effaeba393dedb1a8 (not read; likely the 4.3 backport) and Rails-side fixes (GHSA-wh98-p28r-vrc9, not read). The leak needs Rails before 7.0.2.2 or the matching 6.1, 6.0 and 5.2 patch releases; upgrading either side removes it. Blind audit of lib/puma should find the skipped close; the Rails dependency on close is the stated contract of Rack::BodyProxy.

root_cause: In sudoedit mode resolve_editor() split the user-controlled SUDO_EDITOR, VISUAL or EDITOR value into the editor and its arguments without rejecting a -- argument, while the sudo front end later split the approved command at the first -- to find the files to edit, so paths after a -- inside the editor value became files to edit after the sudoers policy had approved only the command-line files.
audit_scope: plugins/sudoers/editor.c, plugins/sudoers/sudoers.c and the sudoedit front end under src/
notes: Affects sudo 1.8.0 through 1.9.12p1; fixed in 1.9.12p2 (January 2023). The fix rejects a -- argument in the user's editor in resolve_editor(). The front-end code that splits at -- was not changed by the fix and its function name was not confirmed, so it is not listed in symbols.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: DOMPurify.sanitize() checked the parsed DOM tree and returned serialized markup without limiting element nesting depth, so when the browser parsed the output again, its HTML parser's nesting limit restructured deeply nested elements and markup the sanitizer had judged inert ended up in an active context (mutation XSS).
notes: Fixed in 3.1.3 and 2.5.0. c5369f2 is the first commit of PR 943 (adds MAX_NESTING_DEPTH and removes nodes past it); later commits in the PR add the __depth field, cover templates and shadow DOM, and count removed nodes. The 2.x fix is commit 0ef5e537 (short hash, not read). The advisory warns that backports must also take the related fix for CVE-2024-45801 (GHSA-mmhx-hmjr-r674), a separate sample. fixed_ref 3.1.3 is the release named in the advisory.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The ServiceAccount admission plugin was registered only for Create operations and shouldIgnore() skipped every pod subresource, so pod updates through the ephemeralcontainers subresource never went through the kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets check, and ephemeral containers could reference secrets that the annotation-declared policy did not allow.
notes: Fixed in kube-apiserver 1.27.3, 1.26.6, 1.25.11 and 1.24.15. The same commit also fixes CVE-2023-2727 (ImagePolicyWebhook bypass through ephemeral containers) in plugin/pkg/admission/imagepolicy; that is a separate root cause location and is not part of this sample. The fix adds limitEphemeralContainerSecretReferences(). Only affects clusters that use the enforce-mountable-secrets annotation.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
root_cause: ServerOptions kept reject_remote_clients as the PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS bit inside its pipe_mode field, and ServerOptions::pipe_mode() assigned the whole field from the chosen pipe type, so calling pipe_mode() after reject_remote_clients(true), or relying on its secure default, silently cleared the flag and the pipe accepted remote clients.
notes: Windows only. Affects 1.7.0 up to the fixes in 1.18.4, 1.20.3 and 1.23.1 (all 1.24.0 and later are fixed). PR 5336 was merged into the tokio-1.18.x branch; 9ca156c is the fix commit and the other PR commit only prepares the 1.18.4 release. Remote access needs the pipe path to be reachable over SMB. RUSTSEC-2023-0001 covers the same issue (not read).

root_cause: When a client pulled from a server, the client's recv_files() acted on the basis-file selector sent by the server, including fuzzy matching that the client had not enabled and alternate-basis relative paths, and opened the resulting basis file with do_open() without confining it to the destination tree, so a malicious server could make the client checksum arbitrary local files and leak their contents through the checksum exchange.
audit_scope: receiver.c and the basis-file handling it calls (rsync top-level C sources)
notes: Fixed in rsync 3.4.0 (January 2025) by several commits: 8ad4b5d (refuse fuzzy operations when fuzzy was not selected) and c35e283 (open the basis file with secure_relative_open()) were read; b4a27ca (adds secure_relative_open()) and 9f86ddc (disallow ../ in the relative path) are known only by short hash from the commit list and were not read. Order of the commits was not confirmed, so vulnerable_ref is the parent of 8ad4b5d only. The same disclosure has five other rsync CVEs with different root causes.

root_cause: BlockPool.SetPeerRange() accepted every base and height a peer reported and raised the pool's maximum peer height from it without rejecting a later report lower than the peer's earlier one, and the maximum was not recomputed from the lowered value, so one malicious peer could set a sync target no peer would serve and leave the node stuck in blocksync.
notes: Refs are for the v0.38.x line: 2cebfde changes blocksync/pool.go (fixed in v0.38.17). On v1.x the same fix is 0ee80cd in internal/blocksync/pool.go (fixed in v1.0.1). The fix removes and bans a peer that reports a lower height or base than before. Severity was later lowered to Low. Reactor.Receive is listed as affected by GO-2025-3442 but was not changed by the fix.
